title: nashsu/llm_wiki
claim: nashsu/llm_wiki — LLM Wiki is a cross-platform desktop application that turns your documents into an organized, interlinked knowledge base
why_good: Turns local documents into an auto-interlinked, LLM-organized knowledge base on the desktop — a private, offline take on the Notion/Obsidian-AI wave.
value: Someone whose documents cannot legally go to a cloud model — a solo lawyer, an accountant, a clinician. One-off desktop licence, priced against an afternoon of hunting through folders.
risk: The moat is the setup experience, and setup experiences are exactly what a well-funded incumbent copies in one release.
pick_reason: The project offers a clear product that addresses a specific need in information management, making it monetizable.

zh.claim: nashsu/llm_wiki —— 跨平台桌面应用,把你的文档变成有组织、互相链接的知识库。
zh.why_good: 在桌面把本地文档自动互链、用 LLM 组织成知识库——Notion/Obsidian-AI 浪潮里一个私密、离线的做法。
zh.value: 文档在合规上不能上云的人：单打独斗的律师、会计、医生。桌面买断，对标「一下午在文件夹里翻找」。
zh.risk: 护城河是安装体验，而安装体验正是有钱的在位者一个版本就抄走的东西。
zh.hook: 一个人的笔记本里躺着十年的文档，却没有办法向它们提问——四个月 15819 星，219 个未关 issue 里就是这批人卡在配 API key。
zh.does: 桌面应用：读你指定的一个文件夹，自己把里面的文档织成一部互相链接的 wiki，而不是常见的「检索再回答」——它会写词条、会互相引用，于是你是在翻、在问，不是在搜。全程在本机跑，模型你自己接，云端或局域网 Ollama 都行。
zh.gap: 痛点是真的，但前五分钟只有极客过得去。真正需要它的是律师、研究生、硬盘里全是 PDF 的研究者——而 issue 区里挤满了这批人：模型配不上、文件夹选不了、局域网 Ollama 连不通，还没看到第一页 wiki 就走了。
zh.counter: Obsidian、Notion 和每一个笔记应用今年都在发同一个功能，而文档本来就在他们手里。33 位贡献者对 219 个未关 issue，这条线在往坏的方向走；「把我的文件夹变成 wiki」是个演示一次很惊艳、活不过第二周的东西。
zh.differentiator: 卖前五分钟，不卖引擎。签名安装包＋自带能用的模型（或厂商替你出一把 key），一条「指一个文件夹，十分钟后拿到 wiki」的固定路径，并挑一个具体职业做首发切口——从卷宗审阅开始，那批文档在制度上就不许上云。冷启动（中文）：llm_wiki 的 issue 区，以及 #158 里用户自己拉起来的微信群——他们已经在自组织了；冷启动（英文）：r/ObsidianMD 与 r/LocalLLaMA 搜 ask my own documents offline。
zh.why_use: 硬盘里塞满 PDF、却再也找不到任何东西的人：研究生、单干的律师、接手了一堆公司文件的人。他拿到的是一本能翻的 wiki，不是一个还得他自己会问的聊天框。
zh.edge: 检索增强一次只回答一个问题，语料本身仍然是一团。把整本 wiki 先写出来——词条、互链、一张能逛的地图——是长上下文便宜到可以把每份文档读两遍之后才谈得上的事。

zh.consumer_angle: 用的人是自己电脑里堆了几百份文档的普通人：合同、说明书、课件、聊天导出。他拿到的是一本能翻、能问、能引用的本地维基，而不是一个搜索框。

hook: A person with ten years of documents on their own laptop and no way to ask them a question — 15.8k stars in four months, and 219 open issues where those same people are stuck on an API key.

does: A desktop app that reads a folder of your documents and builds an interlinked wiki out of them by itself, instead of the usual retrieve-then-answer trick: it writes entries and cross-links them, so you browse and ask rather than search. Runs on your machine, points at whatever model you configure — cloud or a local Ollama.
gap: It hits a real pain but the first five minutes are geek-only. The person who needs this is a lawyer, a graduate student, a researcher with a hard drive full of PDFs — and the tracker is full of them failing at model configuration, folder selection and LAN Ollama endpoints before they ever see a wiki page.
counter: Obsidian, Notion and every note app are shipping the same feature this year, and they already hold the documents. 219 open issues against 33 contributors is a maintenance line going the wrong way, and 'turn my folder into a wiki' is a demo that dazzles once and then has to survive the second week.
differentiator: Sell the first five minutes, not the engine. A signed installer with a working model bundled or one paid key on the vendor's account, an opinionated 'point at this folder, get a wiki in ten minutes' path, and a single named profession as the launch wedge (start with case-file review, where the documents are private by obligation and cloud AI is disallowed). Cold start (Chinese): the llm_wiki issue tracker and the self-organised WeChat group its users opened in issue #158 — they are already assembling without the maintainer; Cold start (English): r/ObsidianMD and r/LocalLLaMA, search 'ask my own documents offline'.
consumer_angle: Non-developer user: a professional with a private document pile. Finished thing: a browsable, askable wiki of their own files that never leaves the laptop.
why_use: Someone with a hard drive of PDFs they can no longer find anything in — a graduate student, a solo lawyer, a person who inherited a company's paperwork. What they walk away with is a wiki they can browse, not a chatbot they have to interrogate.
edge: Retrieval-augmented search answers one question at a time and leaves the corpus shapeless. Writing the whole wiki up front — entries, cross-links, a map you can wander — only became affordable when long-context reading got cheap enough to pass over every document twice.
